name: Tehar
subtitle: turmeric-yellow rice scented with hing and whole spices, the pandit festival plate

ingredients.qty: 300g, rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: generous ghee is the point of tehar
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse the rice in four changes of water and soak it 20 minutes, then drain in a sieve for 10 minutes so the grains are damp but not wet.
Measure the water exactly — tehar should be dry and separate, not sticky, and there is no rescuing it once it is wet.
Have the turmeric and hing measured into a small bowl together; the tempering takes under a minute.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds, cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf.
steps.tip: The cumin should sizzle and darken by a shade within 15 seconds, not sit silently.

steps.text: Add the broken red chillies and then the asafoetida; it will foam and smell savoury almost at once.
steps.tip: Count three seconds and move on. Burnt hing tastes of nothing but bitterness.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric off the heat so it blooms in the ghee without scorching, about 10 seconds.
Add the drained rice and turn it gently in the yellow ghee for 2 minutes until every grain is coated and glossy.
steps.tip: Use a flat spatula and fold rather than stir; soaked grains snap easily.

steps.text: Pour in the water, add the salt and bring to a hard boil.
As soon as the surface water has been absorbed and craters appear, about 6 minutes, turn the heat to its lowest setting.
Cover tightly and cook undisturbed for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: No lifting the lid. If your lid is loose, weight it with a plate.

steps.text: Take off the heat and stand covered for a further 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, lifting from the base, and serve hot with yogurt or a dry mutton dish.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with 2 tbsp water sprinkled over, on low heat for 6 minutes or in a steamer basket.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
